answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake for a cooling-off period before its votes or reputation count. The system caps influence by stake and slashes it when identities coordinate provably fraudulent transactions, while honest agents recover their stake after review. A sybil farmer must therefore fund many separate deposits and keep capital immobilized; creating cheap names no longer creates cheap influence. A saffron thread or falcon can label an example account, but neither label substitutes for the costly stake.
